title: Reduced Photocurrent from Cracked Photoanode
introduction: Reduced photocurrent from a cracked photoanode is the electrical performance loss in dye-sensitized solar cells (DSSCs) that results when crack networks disrupt the TiO2 electron transport layer. The TiO2 photoanode provides the porous semiconductor network through which photo-generated electrons travel from the dye sensitizer to the external circuit. When EPD-fabricated TiO2 layers contain cracks induced by pore stress concentration, the electron transport pathways are broken or lengthened, reducing the collection efficiency of photo-generated charges. The measurable outcome is a decrease in short-circuit current (Isc) and a reduction in overall conversion efficiency.
reasoning: The 697-Elsevier DSSC study directly reports decreased Isc and conversion efficiency as the performance consequence of cracking in EPD-fabricated TiO2 layers, establishing this as a distinct performance loss node.

key_findings.claim: Cracks in EPD-fabricated TiO2 layers cause a decrease in short-circuit current and overall DSSC conversion efficiency
key_findings.detail: A decrease in short-circuit current (Isc) and efficiency is directly attributed to the TiO2 layer thickness and the cracks appearing in the TiO2 layer fabricated by the EPD technique. [^elsevier697a] These cracks result in decreasing overall conversion efficiency of the DSSC, as disrupted electron transport pathways reduce photo-generated charge collection. [^elsevier697b]

source_locations.quote: A decrease in short circuit current (Isc) and efficiency due to the TiO2 layer thickness and the cracks appearing in the layer fabricated with EPD technique.
These cracks would result in decreasing of overall conversion efficiency of DSSC.
